title: Modular Contract Add‑On: Dynamic Subprocessor & Retention Options
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise prospects frequently stall on negotiation because our contracts bundle multiple residency and data controls together (e.g., subprocessor visibility, retention windows, EU/UK SCC activation). Sales asks for more combinable options and price transparency.

Goal: Design and validate a modular contract add-on flow that lets customers select discrete data-residency/security options at signup or during negotiation, with a corresponding price delta. Provide clear defaults for hosted vs dedicated vs private, automate SCC activation for EU/UK where required, and enable self-serve toggles for low-risk options. Measure impact on deal velocity, attach rate, and ARR.

Scope:
- Product: contract UI in Console and Contract Wizard (selection matrix for Subprocessors, Retention, Geo-lock, SCCs activation).
- Legal/Policy: standardized clause language for each add-on, pre-vetted by Legal to reduce bespoke redlines.
- Pricing: experiment with modular SKUs (flat monthly uplift + per-GB storage) and discount thresholds for bundles.
- Engineering: contract flags, telemetry for selections, billing integration, and gating for Private deployments.
- Sales/RevOps: enable quoting templates and playbook.

Out of scope for this ticket: full on-prem installation packaging and FIPS/HSM procurement details (handled by Private platform workstream).

Success metrics (baseline + target within 8 weeks):
- Decrease average negotiation cycle for residency-related deals by 20%.
- >25% attach rate for modular residency add-ons on new enterprise signups in pilot region.
- <5% incremental legal redlines introduced by add-on language.

Notes on legal constraints: SCCs must be properly triggered for EU/UK customers (auto-selection when billing address or contract jurisdiction is EU/UK). Subprocessor disclosures require attestation flows and a refresh cadence (30/90/180 days depending on customer tier). Retention tiers: 30d, 90d, 365d, custom (enterprise-only).

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: Too many options increases support overhead. Mitigation: default sensible bundles and a ‘recommended for your use-case’ suggestion engine in Console.
- Risk: Pricing complexity confuses sales. Mitigation: pre-built quote templates and a revenue playbook with A/B pricing guidance.
- Risk: Legal review backlog. Mitigation: pre-approved clause library and rolling approvals with Legal Ops triage.

acceptance_criteria: Console contract wizard surfaces modular residency options with help text and default bundle suggestion.
Selections persist to a contract metadata object and are visible to Sales and Legal in the deal view.
Telemetry events emitted for selection, acceptance, and change (for analytics).
Pricing engine supports at least two add-on SKUs and returns an uplifted quote for the customer.
Legal approved clause set stored in Clause Library and linked from the wizard.
Pilot enabled for 3 accounts with measurement dashboard capturing attach rate and negotiation cycle time.
decisions: Use modular add-ons (selectable options) rather than a large set of pre-baked tiers to maximize combinability.
Auto-activate SCCs based on contract jurisdiction with opt-out only after Legal approval (opt-out not self-serve).
Offer retention tiers as discrete SKUs: 30d, 90d, 365d, custom (custom requires contract amendment + Legal sign-off).
Price model: base monthly uplift + per-GB storage fee for retention beyond 90 days.
